chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment for goods) regarding the merchandise when you describe the length and the width.

key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam, a forward sale contract where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered later.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Salam contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions for the validity of the Salam contract, a forward sale prevalent in early Islamic commerce, by mandating precise description of goods to eliminate gharar (uncertainty). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual clarity, distinguishing permissible trade from speculative uncertainty, and underscores the practical necessity of defining physical attributes like length and width to ensure fairness between buyer and seller.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with the retainer regarding the goods when the length and the width are described’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Advance payment to receive goods at an appointed time in the future is lawful if the length and width are fully described.”’
